title: Measuring the Conservatism of Latent Safety Filters for World Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.23685v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe. Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability. However, the filter can still be conservative and refuse many safe actions, depending on the latent. To measure the conservatism that a latent forces on the filter, we group similar latents and actions into cells. A filter that gives one decision per cell can refuse the unsafe transitions of a cell only by refusing the safe ones in it as well. We call the share of safe transitions that lie in such cells the overlap. We prove that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that such a filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data. Both the overlap and the conformal calibration can be applied to any latent. We use this to compare three existing designs, in which the safety labels train

translated_title: 测量世界模型潜在安全过滤器的保守性
translated_abstract: 潜在安全过滤器根据世界模型的潜在表示来判断一个规划的动作是否安全。共形校准通过设置过滤器的阈值，使其仅以很小的概率接受不安全的动作。然而，取决于潜在表示的质量，过滤器仍可能过于保守而拒绝许多安全的动作。为了测量潜在表示强加给过滤器的保守性，我们将相似的潜在表示和动作分组为单元。一个对每个单元只能给出单一决策的过滤器，若要拒绝某单元中的不安全转移，就必须同时拒绝该单元中的安全转移。我们将位于此类单元中的安全转移所占的比例称为“重叠度”。我们证明，重叠度是此类过滤器为了不接受数据中任何不安全转移而必须拒绝的安全转移的最小比例。重叠度和共形校准都可以应用于任何潜在表示。我们利用这一点来比较三种现有设计，其中安全标签用于训练……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了“重叠度”这一指标来衡量世界模型潜在安全过滤器因潜在表示不可区分而被迫拒绝安全动作的最小比例，从而可以量化并比较不同潜在表示设计的保守性。
en_tdlr: Introduces "overlap" as a measure of the minimum share of safe transitions that a latent safety filter must refuse due to indistinguishable latents in a world model, enabling quantification and comparison of conservatism across different latent representation designs.
